issues.text: Design S4 claimed the public backlog would NOT modify the reconciled tenant-default ledger, but 1143_iss0646_fix_gbl133_ledger_poisoning.sql deleted the 5 rows 1107..1111 (iss0122/audit-chain, all_schemas) from tenant_default during the first migrate. Root cause: design B-2 inserts all 111 rows in one transaction sharing a single NOW() applied_at, which exactly matches the GBL-133 poisoning signature (>=2 of the 5 target rows sharing one timestamp) that 1143 is designed to delete. On the healthy test DB these 5 rows have DISTINCT timestamps (genuine per-file applies) so 1143 leaves them; the dev-DB removal was a false positive. Resolved within design intent: re-ran the idempotent reconciliation (S3.6) to restore the canonical 111; 1143's public + tenant_default rows are recorded and the default tenant is stamped, so the restored rows persist (confirmed stable across a second migrate). Suggest a design note: B-2 should stamp distinct applied_at values or document the 1143 interaction.
